questions.question: How does Prometheus collect metrics?
options: Applications push metrics to Prometheus over gRPC
Prometheus pulls (scrapes) HTTP /metrics endpoints on an interval
questions.explanation: Prometheus is pull-based: it scrapes targets' /metrics endpoints (default every 15s). Pull makes 'is the target up?' trivial (the `up` metric) and centralizes control. Short-lived jobs that can't be scraped use the Pushgateway exception.

questions.question: Which metric type should represent 'total HTTP requests served'?
questions.explanation: A counter increases monotonically (resets on restart). Totals-that-only-grow are counters; you derive per-second throughput with rate(). A gauge would be right for a value that goes both ways, like active connections.

questions.question: Why is `rate(http_requests_total[5m])` used instead of the raw counter value?
options: The raw value is a meaningless ever-growing total; rate() converts it to per-second throughput and handles counter resets
rate() is required syntax for all metrics
questions.explanation: '12,483,220 requests since restart' answers nothing. rate() computes the per-second increase over the window and corrects for restarts, yielding the operationally meaningful req/s.

questions.question: What is an exporter?
options: A tool that exports dashboards to PDF
A process that translates a system's internals (host stats, Postgres, etc.) into a Prometheus /metrics endpoint
questions.explanation: Systems that don't speak Prometheus natively get a sidecar translator: node_exporter for host metrics, postgres_exporter, blackbox_exporter for probing endpoints. Prometheus scrapes the exporter like any target.

questions.question: What does `for: 10m` in an alert rule accomplish?
options: The condition must hold continuously for 10 minutes before firing — filtering transient blips
Limits the alert's lifetime to 10 minutes
questions.explanation: The alert sits in 'pending' until the expression has been true for the duration, then fires. It's the main defense against paging on a 30-second spike that self-heals.

questions.question: Which PromQL computes p99 latency from a histogram?
questions.explanation: Histogram quantiles come from bucket counters: rate the buckets, aggregate preserving the `le` label, then histogram_quantile interpolates. Averages hide tail pain — p99 is what your unluckiest 1% of users feel.

questions.question: The `up` metric equals 1 when Prometheus's last scrape of a target succeeded, and 0 when it failed.
questions.explanation: True. Prometheus synthesizes `up` for every target — the built-in heartbeat. `up == 0` (with a short `for:`) is the canonical target-down alert.

questions.question: Adding a user_id label to a request metric is a good way to debug per-user issues.
questions.explanation: False. Every label combination creates a separate time series; unbounded values (user IDs, full URLs, request IDs) explode cardinality until Prometheus runs out of memory. Per-user debugging belongs in logs and traces; labels must be low-cardinality.

questions.question: Your team gets paged on 'CPU > 80%' nightly during backups; users are unaffected and on-call is burning out. What's the principled fix?
options: Alert on user-facing symptoms (error rate, latency SLO burn) and demote resource causes to non-paging warnings/dashboards
Add a second on-call to share the load
questions.explanation: CPU% is a cause, not a symptom — high CPU with healthy latency needs nobody awake. Page on what users experience (golden signals, SLO burn rate); keep saturation metrics as tickets/dashboards for capacity planning.

questions.question: During a database outage, on-call receives 47 alerts from every dependent service. Which Alertmanager features tame this?
options: Grouping (one notification per group) and inhibition (suppress downstream alerts while the root-cause alert fires)
questions.explanation: Grouping collapses related alerts into a single notification; inhibition rules mute symptom alerts while the causal alert (DatabaseDown) is active. 47 pages become one actionable page with context.

questions.question: Write the curl command to fetch node_exporter's metrics endpoint on localhost (default port 9100).
questions.explanation: Every Prometheus target is inspectable with plain curl — the first debugging step when a target shows as down or a metric seems missing: can I even reach /metrics?

questions.question: Write the PromQL expression for the per-second rate of http_requests_total over the last 5 minutes.
questions.explanation: rate(<counter>[window]) is the single most-used PromQL construct: per-second average increase over the window, reset-aware. Wider windows smooth more but react slower.

questions.question: What are the 'four golden signals'?
questions.explanation: From Google's SRE book: how slow (latency), how much (traffic), how broken (errors), how full (saturation). CPU/memory/disk are saturation inputs — components of one signal, not the full picture.

questions.question: What is an error budget?
options: The infrastructure cost allocated to failures
The allowed unreliability implied by an SLO (e.g., 99.9% ⇒ 0.1% of requests may fail) — spent on incidents and risky changes
The number of alerts allowed per week
questions.explanation: The budget converts reliability into a spendable quantity: burning it fast triggers burn-rate alerts and slows releases; budget to spare licenses faster shipping. It replaces 'never break' with an explicit, measurable risk contract.

questions.question: In Grafana, what do template variables (e.g., $namespace, $instance) enable?
options: One dashboard reused across many services/hosts via dropdown selection instead of per-service copies
questions.explanation: Variables interpolate into every panel's query, so a single golden-signals dashboard serves the whole fleet. Copied-per-service dashboards drift and rot; templated ones stay maintained.
